subject: Infra telemetry qualification & competitive follow-up (Redwood vs hyperscalers)
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@atlasfinance.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 18 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Infra telemetry qualification & competitive follow-up (Redwood vs hyperscalers)

Alex — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum with Atlas Finance (summary + specific asks).

Recap (what we heard):
- Primary focus: observability and tracing parity with your current hyperscaler endpoints (trace correlation, request->token cost attribution, service-level dashboards).
- Secondary: predictable p95 latency for interactive sessions and cost modeling (batched workloads).
- Compliance/attestation: you requested SOC 2 artifacts and audit log retention details for a later procurement review.

Where Redwood stands (summary differentiators briefly):
- Unified traces + token-level cost: our console can show token breakdown by route + correlated trace ID — this is what most hyperscalers surface via custom logging + sampling, but Redwood exposes this out of the box and ties it to model variant routing and cache hits.
- Automated KV/prefix caching telemetry: we'll surface cache hit rates and their per-route cost impact (helps justify quantization/batching trade-offs).
- Rollback & fallback observability: our rollout traces include fallback reasons and capacity-tier routing to diagnose degradations without diving into infra logs.

Proposed qualification tests (small, time-boxed):
1) Trace correlation test (owner: Redwood engineering / Marissa): instrument 5 representative requests and confirm end-to-end trace IDs across your app -> Redwood -> model runtime. Success criteria: trace spans present + latency annotation at token boundaries.
2) Cost attribution experiment (owner: Redwood sales + Atlas Eng): replay a 1k-token mixed session (interactive + batch) and compare per-call token accounting and total unit cost vs your hyperscaler baseline. Success criteria: per-call token delta <= 10% after normalizing batching differences.
3) Observability dashboard check (owner: Redwood Ops / Sergio): provision a short-lived demo route and validate dashboards for p50/p95 latency, request breakdown, cache hits, and alerting (example: p95 > 350ms triggers).

Logistics / asks from Atlas:
- Can you share a short trace sample (redacted) or an example request/response payload so we can pre-build the trace-correlation shim? (attachment: trace-sample-annotation.txt)
- Who should we loop in for procurement? You mentioned Kai — can we include them on next notes?
- Preferred window for a 90-min POC kickoff next week (we can run the three tests across a day).

Attachments: redwood-vs-hyperscalers-telemetry-matrix.xlsx (workbook shows the telemetry mapping + proposed test checklist)

Next steps I propose:
- Alex confirms procurement contact + preferred POC date
- Redwood to prepare a lightweight test harness and a minimal tracing shim (Marissa)
- Redwood to provision a demo route and share Drive folder with runbook (Sergio)

Thanks — will be brief and scoped so you can compare apples-to-apples.

— Ben

From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@atlasfinance.com>

Date: Sat, 18 Jul 2026 12:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Infra telemetry qualification & competitive follow-up (Redwood vs hyperscalers)

Ben — appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Top priority is the trace correlation + cost attribution. We currently stitch request IDs in our frontend to the hyperscaler traces, but it's manual and the cost breakdown requires correlating logs with billing exports. If Redwood can show token-level charge attribution and map that to our request IDs, that's a big win.
- For the cost test, we care less about absolute % difference and more about consistent, reproducible measurement. Let's add an item: how stable is token accounting under variable batch sizes (you suggested we test 1, 4, 16).
- Procurement: Kai (cc'd) will handle procurement/contract items — Kai, please confirm the standard proof points you need (SOC 2, Data Residency, retention windows).

Availability: next week Tue/Wed morning ET works for the kickoff. We can schedule a 90-min slot for the setup/test run.

Also attaching one redacted trace export (we'll email separately — security) and Kai will send procurement checklist.

Thanks,
Alex

Atlas Finance

Subject: Fwd: Infra telemetry qualification & competitive follow-up (action items)

Folks — forwarding Alex's note. Quick internal split of work so we can move fast: 

Marissa (eng): build the tracing shim and test harness. Tasks:
- Create a tiny instrumentation library that accepts Atlas request_id and emits a Redwood trace span mapping. Provide example curl/JS snippets.
- Validate trace span includes token-boundary annotations and model-variant metadata.
- Target: have a trace sample captured by Monday EOD PT.

Sergio (ops/POC infra): provisioning + dashboards. Tasks: 
- Provision a demo route with an identical model variant that Atlas will use for test (short-lived).
- Create a dashboard in the console with p50/p95, cache hit rate, token cost column, and an alert rule: p95 > 350ms (for interactive route).
- Drop a runbook in the shared Drive folder and attach the telemetry matrix.

Ben (me): coordinate scheduling, capture requirements from Kai, and own comparative cost sheet. I'll validate the experiment parameters (batch sizes: 1, 4, 16) before the run.

Please reply with any issues or if you need a scope change. I want this to be a narrow win — short POC, measurable results.

Thanks,
— Ben
